value.event: Jia Nanfeng's dominance to his execution (outside-knowledge conversion: AD 290-AD 300)
Han Shou was the proposed father-in-law in Guo Huai's marriage plan; no calendar date is stated.
Han Shou's daughter was proposed as heir apparent's consort
Han Shou's son was taken by the empress to substitute for the heir apparent

title.zh: 卷三十一 列傳第一 后妃上
title.en: Volume 31 Biographies 1: Empresses and Consorts Part One
title.raw: 卷三十一 列傳第一 后妃上 Volume 31 Biographies 1: Empresses and Consorts Part One

sentences.zh: 惠賈皇后諱南風，平陽人也，小名時。

translations.literal: Empress Jia of Hui, taboo Nanfeng, native of Pingyang, childhood name Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jia Nanfeng of Pingyang—pet name Shi.

sentences.zh: 父充，別有傳。

translations.literal: Her father Chong has separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Jia Chong has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 初，武帝欲為太子取衛瓘女，元后納賈郭親黨之說，欲婚賈氏。

translations.literal: At first Emperor Wu wished crown prince to marry Wei Guan’s daughter; Empress Yuan listened to Jia and Guo faction urging marriage with Jia clan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu favored Wei Guan’s daughter; Empress Yang Yan pushed Jia kin.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「衛公女有五可，賈公女有五不可。

translations.literal: Emperor said: “Lord Wei’s daughter has five goods—Lord Jia’s daughter five bads.
translations.idiomatic: Wu said, “Wei’s girl scores five merits—Jia’s five flaws.

sentences.zh: 衛家種賢而多子，美而長白；

translations.literal: Wei house breeds wise and many sons—beautiful, tall, fair;
translations.idiomatic: Weis are fertile and wise—fair and statuesque;

sentences.zh: 賈家種妒而少子，醜而短黑。」

translations.literal: Jia house breeds jealousy and few sons—ugly, short, dark.”
translations.idiomatic: Jias are jealous and barren—dark and squat."

sentences.zh: 元后固請，荀顗、荀勖並稱充女之賢，乃定婚。

translations.literal: Empress Yuan pressed firmly—Xun Yi and Xun Xu together praised Chong’s daughter’s virtue—betrothal fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan insisted; Xun Yi and Xun Xu praised Jia’s girl—the match closed.

sentences.zh: 始欲聘后妹午，午年十二，小太子一歲，短小未勝衣。

translations.literal: At first they wished to engage younger sister Wu—Wu twelve years old, one year younger than crown prince, too short for robes.
translations.idiomatic: They first chose sister Wu—twelve, petite beside the heir.

sentences.zh: 更娶南風，時年十五，大太子二歲。

translations.literal: They switched to Nanfeng—then fifteen, two years elder than crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: They wed Nanfeng instead—fifteen, two years his senior.

sentences.zh: 泰始八年二月辛卯[7]，冊拜太子妃。

translations.literal: Eighth Taishi year second month xinmao [7]—invested crown princess.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao in early 272 she became crown princess [7].

sentences.zh: 妒忌多權詐，太子畏而惑之，嬪御罕有進幸者。

translations.literal: Jealous, crafty in intrigue—crown prince feared yet dazed—concubines rarely gained favor.
translations.idiomatic: Jealous and scheming, she cowed the befuddled prince—other women seldom touched him.

sentences.zh: 初，后詐有身，內稿物為產具，遂取妹夫韓壽子慰祖養之，託諒闇所生，故弗顯。

translations.literal: At first consort feigned pregnancy—packed straw goods as birthing gear—then took sister’s husband Han Shou’s son Weizu raising—claimed mourning-hall birth—therefore not openly shown.
translations.idiomatic: She faked pregnancy—snatched Han Shou’s son Weizu—called him newborn heir.

sentences.zh: 遂謀廢太子，以所養代立。

translations.literal: Then plotted depose crown prince—establish fosterling.
translations.idiomatic: She meant to replace the heir with him.

sentences.zh: 時洛中謠曰：「南風烈烈吹黃沙，遙望魯國鬱嵯峨，前至三月滅汝家。」

translations.literal: Then Luoyang rhyme said: "South wind fierce blows yellow sand—far gaze Lu kingdom towering—before third month ends your house."
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang sang: "Nanfeng blasts yellow dust—far off Lu towers loom—by the third moon your house will fall."

sentences.zh: 后母廣城君以后無子，甚敬重愍懷，每勸厲后，使加慈愛。

translations.literal: Consort mother Lady Guangcheng because consort lacked sons greatly revered Crown Prince Minhuai—often urged consort—made her add kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Guo prized Minhuai—begged Jia to cherish him.

sentences.zh: 賈謐恃貴驕縱，不能推崇太子，廣城君恒切責之。

translations.literal: Jia Mi relied on pride—could not honor crown prince—Lady Guangcheng constantly scolded.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Mi insulted the heir—Lady Guo scolded him.

sentences.zh: 及廣城君病篤，占術謂不宜封廣城，乃改封宜城。

translations.literal: When Lady Guangcheng gravely ill—divination said unsuitable enfeoff Guangcheng—thereupon changed enfeoff Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ill diviners forbade “Guangcheng”—she became Princess Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 后出侍疾十餘日，太子常往宜城第，將醫出入，恂恂盡禮。

translations.literal: Consort attended illness ten-plus days—crown prince often visited Yicheng mansion—brought physicians—obedient exhaustive ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Minhuai nursed her mother—deferential.

sentences.zh: 宜城臨終執后手，令盡意于太子，言甚切至。

translations.literal: Yicheng dying grasped consort’s hand—ordered exhaust feeling toward crown prince—speech extremely earnest.
translations.idiomatic: She clasped Jia’s hand—beg her shield Minhuai.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「趙粲及午必亂汝事，我死後，勿復聽入，深憶吾言。」

translations.literal: Also said: “Zhao Can and Wu surely ruin your affairs—after I die—never hear them again—deeply remember my words.”
translations.idiomatic: She also said, "Zhao Can and Jia Wu will surely disrupt your affairs; after I die, do not admit them again—remember my words well."

sentences.zh: 后不能遵之，遂專制天下，威服內外。

translations.literal: Consort could not obey—thereupon monopolized realm—awe subdued inner and outer.
translations.idiomatic: Jia ignored—ruled alone.

sentences.zh: 更與粲、午專為姦謀，誣害太子，眾惡彰著。

translations.literal: Further with Can, Wu solely plotted wickedness—slandered harmed crown prince—crowds of evils manifest.
translations.idiomatic: She schemed with them against Minhuai.

sentences.zh: 初，誅楊駿及汝南王亮、太保衛瓘、楚王瑋等，皆臨機專斷，宦人董猛參預其事。

translations.literal: At first executing Yang Jun and Prince Runan Liang, Grand Tutor Wei Guan, Prince Chu Wei—all improvised executions—eunuch Dong Meng participated.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun, Sima Liang, Wei Guan, Sima Wei died by her whim—with eunuch Dong Meng.

sentences.zh: 猛，武帝時為寺人監，侍東宮，得親信于后，預誅楊駿，封武安侯，猛三兄皆為亭侯，天下咸怨。

translations.literal: Meng—Wu-era Inner Palace Overseer—served Eastern Palace—won consort trust—participated executing Yang Jun—enfeoffed Marquis Wu’an—Meng three elder brothers all village marquis—all realm resented.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Meng gained titles—his brothers too—the realm cursed them.

sentences.zh: 及太子廢黜，趙王倫、孫秀等因眾怨謀欲廢后[8]。

translations.literal: When crown prince deposed—Prince Zhao Lun and Sun Xiu exploiting resentment plotted depose consort [8].
translations.idiomatic: Once Minhuai fell Sima Lun and Sun Xiu used hatred to target her [8].

sentences.zh: 后數遣宮婢微服於人間視聽，其謀頗泄。

translations.literal: Consort repeatedly sent palace maids plain clothes among folk spy listen—plot leaked somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: She spied on rumors—some leaked.

sentences.zh: 后甚懼，遂害太子，以絕眾望。

translations.literal: Consort greatly afraid—thereupon harmed crown prince—cutting off hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified she murdered Minhuai.

sentences.zh: 趙王倫乃率兵入宮，使翊軍校尉齊王冏入殿廢后。

translations.literal: Prince Zhao Lun then led troops palace—ordered Colonel Qi Wang Jiong enter hall depose consort.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Lun stormed in—sent Sima Jiong to drag her out.

sentences.zh: 后與冏母有隙，故倫使之。

translations.literal: Consort with Jiong’s mother bore grudge—therefore Lun sent him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong hated her mother—Lun used him.

sentences.zh: 后驚曰：「卿何為來！」

translations.literal: Consort alarmed said: “Why have you come!”
translations.idiomatic: She cried, “Why you!”

sentences.zh: 冏曰：「有詔收后。」

translations.literal: Jiong said: "There is an edict to seize you."
translations.idiomatic: Jiong said, "There is an edict to seize you."

sentences.zh: 后曰：「詔當從我出，何詔也？」

translations.literal: Consort said: "Edicts issue from me—what edict is this?"
translations.idiomatic: She snapped, "Edicts issue from me—what edict is this?"

sentences.zh: 后至上閤，遙呼帝曰：「陛下有婦，使人廢之，亦行自廢。」

translations.literal: Consort reaching upper chamber cried distant emperor: “Your Majesty has wife yet lets others depose her—you yourself will be deposed.”
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the upper chamber she cried to the emperor, "Your Majesty has a wife, yet you let others depose her—you will be deposed yourself."

sentences.zh: 又問冏曰：「起事者誰？」

translations.literal: Again asked Jiong: “Who raised revolt?”
translations.idiomatic: She asked Jiong again, "Who raised this affair?"

sentences.zh: 冏曰：「梁、趙。」

translations.literal: Jiong said: “Liang and Zhao.”
translations.idiomatic: “Liang and Zhao.”

sentences.zh: 后曰：「繫狗當繫頸，今反繫其尾，何得不然！」

translations.literal: Consort said: “Leash dog by throat—now leash tail—how can it not be so!”
translations.idiomatic: “Chain a dog by the throat—you seized the tail—no wonder!”

sentences.zh: 至宮西，見謐尸，再舉聲而哭遽止。

translations.literal: Reaching palace west saw Mi corpse—raised voice twice weeping suddenly stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Jia Mi’s corpse she wailed twice—then silence.

sentences.zh: 倫乃矯詔遣尚書劉弘等持節齎金屑酒賜后死。

translations.literal: Lun then forged edict dispatch Minister Liu Hong bearing tally deliver gold-filings wine grant consort death.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Lun sent Liu Hong with golden liquor.

sentences.zh: 后在位十一年。

translations.literal: Consort held rank eleven years.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven years queen.

sentences.zh: 趙粲、賈午、韓壽、董猛等皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Zhao Can, Jia Wu, Han Shou, Dong Meng executed.
translations.idiomatic: Her cabal died with her.

title.zh: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子
title.raw: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子 Volume 53 Biographies 23: Crown Prince Minhuai

sentences.zh: 太子性剛，知賈謐恃後之貴，不能假借之。

translations.literal: The crown prince's temper was stiff; knowing Jia Mi relied on the empress's power, he would not indulge him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu refused to flatter Jia Mi.

sentences.zh: 謐至東宮，或舍之而於後庭遊戲。

translations.literal: When Mi came to the Eastern Palace he sometimes left him waiting while he played in the inner courts.
translations.idiomatic: He left Jia Mi cooling heels while he played inside.

sentences.zh: 詹事裴權諫曰：「賈謐甚有寵于中宮，而有不順之色，若一旦交構，大事去矣。

translations.literal: Household Superintendent Pei Quan remonstrated: 'Jia Mi is deeply favored in the inner palace yet shows disrespectful looks—if they ever turn on you, the great enterprise is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Household Superintendent Pei Quan remonstrated: "Jia Mi is deeply favored in the inner palace yet shows disrespectful looks—if they ever turn on you, the great enterprise is lost.

sentences.zh: 宜深自謙屈，以防其變，廣延賢士，用自輔翼。」

translations.literal: You should humble yourself deeply to guard against change and broadly recruit worthy men to aid your wings.'
translations.idiomatic: You should humble yourself deeply to guard against change and broadly recruit worthy men to aid your wings."

sentences.zh: 太子不能從。

translations.literal: The crown prince would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yu ignored him.

sentences.zh: 初，賈后母郭槐欲以韓壽女為太子妃，太子亦欲婚韓氏以自固。

translations.literal: Earlier Empress Jia's mother Guo Huai had wished to take Han Shou's daughter as crown princess; the crown prince also wished to marry the Hans to strengthen himself.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Huai once pushed a Han match—Yu wanted it too.

sentences.zh: 而壽妻賈午及後皆不聽，而為太子聘王衍小女惠風。

translations.literal: But Han Shou's wife Jia Wu and the empress both refused and instead betrothed the crown prince to Wang Yan's younger daughter Huifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Wu and the empress forced Wang Yan's younger daughter Huifeng instead.

sentences.zh: 太子聞衍長女美，而賈后為謐聘之，心不能平，頗以為言。

translations.literal: The crown prince heard Wang's elder daughter was beautiful while the empress betrothed her to Jia Mi; his heart could not rest easy and he spoke of it often.
translations.idiomatic: Yu resented losing Wang's elder beauty to Jia Mi.

sentences.zh: 謐嘗與太子圍棋，爭道，成都王穎見而訶謐，謐意愈不平，因此譖太子于後曰：「太子廣買田業，多畜私財以結小人者，為賈氏故也。

translations.literal: Once Mi played go with the crown prince and they quarreled over the move; Ying, Prince of Chengdu, saw and rebuked Mi; Mi grew more resentful and therefore slandered the crown prince to the empress: 'The crown prince buys fields wholesale, hoards private wealth, and courts petty men—all because of the Jia clan.
translations.idiomatic: Once while playing go with the crown prince Mi quarreled over a move; Ying, Prince of Chengdu, saw and rebuked Mi; Mi grew more resentful and slandered the crown prince to the empress: "The crown prince buys fields wholesale, hoards private wealth, and courts petty men—all because of the Jia clan.

sentences.zh: 密聞其言云：'皇后萬歲後，吾當魚肉之。

translations.literal: I have secretly heard him say: "After the empress dies, I shall butcher them."
translations.idiomatic: Mi quoted Yu vowing to slaughter the Jias after Jia died.

sentences.zh: '非但如是也，若宮車晏駕，彼居大位，依楊氏故事，誅臣等而廢後於金墉，如反手耳。

translations.literal: Not only that—if the imperial carriage halts and he reaches the great seat, following Lady Yang's precedent he will execute us ministers and lock you away at Jinyong like turning his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Not only that—if the imperial carriage halts and he reaches the great seat, following Lady Yang's precedent he will execute us ministers and lock you away at Jinyong like turning his hand.

sentences.zh: 不如早為之所，更立慈順者以自防衛。」

translations.literal: Better strike early, remove him, and set up someone kindly and tractable to defend ourselves.'
translations.idiomatic: Better strike early, remove him, and set up someone kindly and tractable to defend ourselves."

sentences.zh: 後納其言，又宣揚太子之短，布諸遠近。

translations.literal: The empress accepted his words and further broadcast the crown prince's faults throughout near and far.
translations.idiomatic: Jia adopted the plot and smeared Yu empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 于時朝野咸知賈后有害太子意。

translations.literal: Then court and countryside knew the empress meant to harm the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone saw Jia meant to kill the heir.

sentences.zh: 中護軍趙俊請太子廢後，太子不聽。

translations.literal: Central Guard Zhao Jun asked the crown prince to depose the empress first; the crown prince refused.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jun urged preemptive deposition—Yu declined.

sentences.zh: 初，廣城君郭槐，以賈后無子，常勸后使慈愛太子。

translations.literal: Earlier the Lady of Guangcheng, Guo Huai, because Empress Jia had no son, often urged the empress to treat the Heir Apparent with kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Guo Huai, Lady of Guangcheng, because Empress Jia had no son of her own, often urged her to treat the heir apparent kindly.

sentences.zh: 賈謐驕縱，數無禮於太子，廣城君恆切責之。

translations.literal: Jia Mi was arrogant and unrestrained, repeatedly disrespectful toward the Heir Apparent; the Lady of Guangcheng constantly rebuked him sharply.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Mi was arrogant and repeatedly insulted the heir apparent. The Lady of Guangcheng scolded him harshly again and again.

sentences.zh: 廣城君欲以韓壽女為太子妃，太子亦欲婚韓氏以自固；

translations.literal: The Lady of Guangcheng wished to make Han Shou's daughter the Heir Apparent's consort; the Heir Apparent also wished to marry into the Han clan to secure himself;
translations.idiomatic: The Lady of Guangcheng wanted Han Shou's daughter as the heir apparent's consort, and the heir apparent likewise hoped to marry into the Han clan to strengthen his position;

sentences.zh: 壽妻賈午及后皆不聽，而為太子聘王衍少女。

translations.literal: Han Shou's wife Jia Wu and the empress would not agree, and instead betrothed to the Heir Apparent the younger daughter of Wang Yan.
translations.idiomatic: but Han Shou's wife Jia Wu and the empress refused and betrothed the heir apparent to Wang Yan's younger daughter instead.

sentences.zh: 太子聞衍長女美，而后為賈謐聘之，心不能平，頗以為言。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent heard that Yan's elder daughter was beautiful, yet the empress betrothed her to Jia Mi; he could not compose his heart and spoke of it with some resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent heard that Yan's elder daughter was beautiful, yet the empress gave her to Jia Mi. He was bitter and complained openly.

sentences.zh: 及廣城君病，臨終，執后手，令盡心於太子，言甚切至。

translations.literal: When the Lady of Guangcheng fell ill, at the end she took the empress's hand and ordered her to devote her heart to the Heir Apparent, her words very earnest.
translations.idiomatic: When the Lady of Guangcheng fell mortally ill, she took the empress's hand at the end and urged her with utmost earnestness to devote herself to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「趙粲、賈午，必亂汝家事；

translations.literal: She also said: "Zhao Can and Jia Wu will surely ruin your household affairs;
translations.idiomatic: She also said: "Zhao Can and Jia Wu will surely ruin your household.

sentences.zh: 我死後，勿復聽入。

translations.literal: after my death, do not again let them enter your counsel.
translations.idiomatic: After I die, do not let them near you again.

sentences.zh: 深記吾言。」

translations.literal: Remember my words deeply."
translations.idiomatic: Remember this well."

sentences.zh: 后不從，更與粲、午謀害太子。

translations.literal: The empress did not obey and instead joined with Can and Wu to plot harm to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The empress ignored her and instead joined Can and Wu in plotting against the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 太子性剛，知賈謐恃中宮驕貴，不能假借之。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent was by nature stern; knowing that Jia Mi relied on the central palace's arrogant eminence, he could not show him favor.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent was proud by nature. Knowing Jia Mi relied on the empress's power, he would not indulge him.

sentences.zh: 謐時為侍中，至東宮，或捨之，於後庭遊戲。

translations.literal: Mi was then Attendant of the Yellow Gate; when he came to the Eastern Palace the Heir Apparent sometimes dismissed him and played in the rear court.
translations.idiomatic: Mi was then Attendant of the Yellow Gate. When he visited the Eastern Palace the heir apparent sometimes dismissed him and amused himself in the rear court.

sentences.zh: 詹事裴權諫曰：「謐，后所親暱，一旦交構，則事危矣。」

translations.literal: The Steward Pei Quan remonstrated: "Mi is one the empress cherishes; if you should clash, the affair would be perilous."
translations.idiomatic: Steward Pei Quan warned him: "Mi is the empress's favorite. If you quarrel with him, disaster will follow."

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: He did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: He would not listen.

sentences.zh: 謐譖太子於后曰：「太子多畜私財以結小人者，為賈氏故也。

translations.literal: Mi slandered the Heir Apparent to the empress, saying: "The Heir Apparent amasses private wealth to win over petty men because of the Jia clan.
translations.idiomatic: Mi slandered the heir apparent to the empress, saying: "He hoards private wealth to win over petty men because he means to destroy the Jia clan.

sentences.zh: 若宮車晏駕，彼居大位，依楊氏故事，誅臣等，廢后於金墉，如反手耳。

translations.literal: If the imperial carriage should halt forever and he take the great position, following the Yang clan precedent he would execute us ministers and depose the empress at Jinyong—it would be like turning the hand.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor dies and he takes the throne, he will follow the Yang clan precedent, execute us, and imprison you at Jinyong. It will be as easy as turning his hand.

sentences.zh: 不如早圖之，更立慈順者，可以自安。」

translations.literal: Better to plot early, set up another who is kindly and obedient, and thus secure ourselves."
translations.idiomatic: Better act early and set up another heir who is mild and obedient. Then we may be safe."

sentences.zh: 后納其言，乃宣揚太子之短，佈於遠近。

translations.literal: The empress accepted his words and thereupon spread abroad the Heir Apparent's faults, broadcasting them far and near.
translations.idiomatic: The empress accepted his counsel and spread the heir apparent's faults far and wide.

sentences.zh: 又詐為有娠，內蒿物、產具，取妹夫韓壽子慰祖養之，欲以代太子。

translations.literal: She also feigned pregnancy, hid artemisia and birthing gear within, took her brother-in-law Han Shou's son Weizu to rear, and intended to replace the Heir Apparent with him.
translations.idiomatic: She also feigned pregnancy, hid birthing supplies inside, took her brother-in-law Han Shou's son Weizu to rear, and planned to replace the heir apparent with him.

title.zh: 卷一百〇九 載記第九 慕容皝
title.raw: 卷一百〇九 載記第九 慕容皝 Volume 109 Records 9: Murong Huang

sentences.zh: 封弈等以皝任重位輕，宜稱燕王，皝於是以咸康三年僭即王位，赦其境內。

translations.literal: Feng Yi and others because Huang’s burden was weighty yet rank was light, ought to style King of Yan; Huang thereupon in the third year of Xiankang illegitimately assumed kingship, pardoned those within his borders.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yi and others, holding that Huang’s burden was heavy while his rank was light, urged him to style himself King of Yan; Huang thereupon in the third year of Xiankang illegitimately assumed the kingship and pardoned those within his borders.

sentences.zh: 以封弈為國相，韓壽為司馬，裴開、陽騖、王寓、李洪、杜群、宋該、劉瞻、石琮、皇甫真、陽協、宋晃、平熙、張泓等並為列卿將帥。

translations.literal: Made Feng Yi state chancellor, Han Shou marshal, Pei Kai, Yang Wu, Wang Yu, Li Hong, Du Qun, Song Gai, Liu Zhan, Shi Cong, Huangfu Zhen, Yang Xie, Song Huang, Ping Xi, Zhang Hong and others concurrently ministers and generals.
translations.idiomatic: He named Feng Yi chancellor, Han Shou marshal, and distributed ministerial and command posts among Pei Kai, Yang Wu, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 起文昌殿，乘金根車，駕六馬，出入稱警蹕。
